title: Scales and degrees
summary: Build major, harmonic minor, melodic minor and chromatic scales, and name scale degrees.

provenance.notes: Items drawn from the seeded generators with a teaching-point filter, then fixed. Music and answers come from the rule engine; prompts and feedback are original.

items.prompt: Write the scale of D major, ascending, in the bass clef. Use accidentals instead of a key signature. The first note is written for you.
hints: One note on every line and space.
Major pattern: tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.

feedback.correct: Beautiful scale: one note on each letter, semitones in the right places.

mistakes.semitone-misplaced: Check the pattern of tones and semitones — the semitones aren't where they belong.
mistakes.letter-skipped-or-repeated: Each letter name appears once. You've used one letter twice and skipped another — respell that note.
mistakes.wrong-minor-form: Check which form of the minor scale is asked for, and which notes that form changes.
mistakes.melodic-descent-not-restored: Coming down, the melodic minor uses the notes of the key signature — undo the raised 6th and 7th.
mistakes.key-signature-misapplied: With a key signature, notes it covers don't need accidentals. Without one, every sharp or flat must be written.
mistakes.wrong-direction-or-octave: Check whether the question asks for ascending or descending, and which octave to start on.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Write one note per letter name first, then check the tones and semitones.

items.prompt: Write the D harmonic minor scale, descending, in the treble clef. Use accidentals instead of a key signature. The first note is written for you.
hints: Harmonic minor: the key-signature notes with the 7th raised a semitone, going up and coming down.

feedback.correct: Correct. Harmonic minor raises the 7th, both ways.

items.prompt: Write the E melodic minor scale, ascending then descending, in the bass clef. Use accidentals instead of a key signature. The first note is written for you.
hints: Melodic: raise 6 and 7 going up; restore them coming down.
Melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th going up, and lowers them again coming down.

feedback.correct: Yes: raised 6th and 7th going up, restored coming down.

items.prompt: Write a chromatic scale ascending from E, one octave, in the treble clef. Use every letter name at least once and no more than twice.
hints: Move by a semitone each time. Between two letters a tone apart, add one note with the same letter as one of them plus an accidental.

feedback.correct: A correct chromatic scale: every semitone, with no letter used more than twice.

mistakes.letter-used-three-times: Each letter name can appear at most twice in a chromatic scale.
mistakes.letter-missing: Every letter name must appear at least once.
mistakes.not-all-semitones: Every step in a chromatic scale is a semitone. Check where the gap is bigger.
mistakes.unnecessary-accidentals: That's correct but harder to read. With this key signature, choose spellings that need fewer accidentals.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Check that each step is a semitone and each letter appears once or twice.

items.prompt: In C major, which degree of the scale is this note?

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave in C major with its key signature, showing D.

hints: Count up the scale of C major from the tonic, C, which is degree 1.

feedback.correct: Right. You counted up from the tonic.

mistakes.counted-from-wrong-note: Count from the tonic (the key note) as degree 1.
mistakes.off-by-one: The tonic itself is degree 1 — count it too.
mistakes.name-number-mismatch: Check the technical name that belongs to that degree number.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Write out the scale from the tonic and count.
